summary.text: Tony Wied is the Republican incumbent for Wisconsin's 8th District. A Green Bay-area businessman who operated Dino Stop gas stations and Little Caesars restaurants until selling the businesses in 2022, he won the 2024 special and general elections with President Trump's endorsement and was sworn in on November 12, 2024. He serves on the Agriculture, Small Business, and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

paragraphs.text: Wied was born in Lincoln, Nebraska, and raised in Green Bay, where his official biography says he has spent his entire life in Northeast Wisconsin.
He graduated from Notre Dame Academy in Green Bay in 1994 and played football at St. Norbert College in De Pere, earning a bachelor's degree in business and administration in 1998.

With his wife, Angela, Wied operated several Dino Stop gas stations and convenience stores in Northeast Wisconsin and later opened several Little Caesars restaurants; the businesses were sold in 2022.

In his Ballotpedia survey he described himself as a political outsider with nearly three decades of experience starting and operating businesses, and said he was the only candidate endorsed by President Trump in the race.
Wied was elected in 2024 to the seat vacated by Mike Gallagher, was sworn in on November 12, 2024, and was elected to a full term in the 119th Congress.
In 2025-2026 he was assigned to the Committee on Agriculture, the Committee on Small Business and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, according to Ballotpedia.
According to his official biography, he lives in De Pere with his wife, Angela, and their four sons.
